ed25519-donna_2015-03-16_gcc13_x64_ed255.license: public domain, as declared in the header of each source file (Andrew M.); the repository ships no licence file
ed25519-donna_2015-03-16_gcc13_x64_ed255.notes: The master HEAD of a repository with no releases, built as ed25519.c compiled straight into a shared object, once as upstream's default code for the target (32-bit on x86, __int128 on x64) and once with -DED25519_SSE2. Uses upstream's reference SHA-512 (ED25519_REFHASH), which Tor replaces with its own digest, so sha512_blocks and the ed25519_hash_* functions are not in a Tor build. ed25519_randombytes_unsafe is the only function not from upstream: a memset stub in scripts/corpus/exercisers, which resolves the symbol ED25519_CUSTOMRANDOM leaves open and must never run. 30 named functions of ten instructions or more in the generic x64 artefacts, 32 in the x86 ones and 33 in the SSE2 ones: the DONNA_INLINE force-inlining does not reduce this - without it the count is within two. Crypto++ 8.x ships a port of part of this code, so about 8 (x64) to 11 (x86) of these functions also match data/cryptopp under its C++ names; libsodium shares none. ED25519_SUFFIX is not set in the plain and SSE2 components, so their symbols are ed25519_publickey and not Tor's ed25519_publickey_donna. The third component, ed25519-donna-tor, is the Tor-style build: ed25519.c built the way Tor builds it (src/ext/include.am): -DED25519_CUSTOMHASH, -DED25519_CUSTOMRANDOM and -DED25519_SUFFIX=_donna, so every public function is ed25519_publickey_donna, ed25519_sign_donna, ed25519_sign_open_donna, ed25519_sign_open_batch_donna and curved25519_scalarmult_basepoint_donna. Tor's digest (crypto_digest_t over libcrypto or NSS) is not a dependency a reference build can have, so the digest is the one scripts/corpus/exercisers/ed25519_donna_tor_hash.h supplies, forced in with -include: upstream's own reference SHA-512 (the code ED25519_REFHASH selects, from the unmodified ed25519-hash.h at the pinned commit, its four public names renamed donna_ref_*) wrapped in Tor's shape, a heap-allocated digest behind a one-pointer context. Upstream's own ed25519-hash-custom.h is an empty comment, so nothing in the upstream tree is changed. It stands in for Tor's digest and says nothing about what libcrypto's SHA-512 compiles to. ed25519_randombytes_unsafe_donna is the memset stub of ed25519_donna_rng.c, named through -DED25519_RNG_NAME, and must never run. Tor's own ed25519_tor.c, with its Tor-specific API (_blind_secret_key, _blind_public_key, _pubkey_from_curve25519_pubkey, ...), is the separate 2026-10-07-tor build from the Tor tree. MinGW x86 36 kept + 53 removed = 89, x64 42 + 53 = 95; Linux x86 57 + 5 = 62, x64 44 + 6 = 50 (33, 31, 36 and 30 functions of ten instructions or more). Against the same-target REFHASH build (the plain ed25519-donna component) the PicHashes at ten instructions or more are shared 29 of 33 (MinGW x86), 29 of 31 (MinGW x64), 21 of 36 (Linux x86) and 27 of 30 (Linux x64); what differs is the digest wrapper and the functions that call it (sign, hram, sign_open_batch on some targets), so a Tor-built sample matches this component on the field and group arithmetic and on the renamed public API, not on the hash.

Uses upstream's reference SHA-512 (ED25519_REFHASH), which Tor replaces with its own digest, so sha512_blocks and the ed25519_hash_* functions are not in a Tor build. ed25519_randombytes_unsafe is the only function not from upstream: a memset stub in scripts/corpus/exercisers, which resolves the symbol ED25519_CUSTOMRANDOM leaves open and must never run. 30 named functions of ten instructions or more in the generic x64 artefacts, 32 in the x86 ones and 33 in the SSE2 ones: the DONNA_INLINE force-inlining does not reduce this - without it the count is within two. Crypto++ 8.x ships a port of part of this code, so about 8 (x64) to 11 (x86) of these functions also match data/cryptopp under its C++ names; libsodium shares none. ED25519_SUFFIX is not set in the plain and SSE2 components, so their symbols are ed25519_publickey and not Tor's ed25519_publickey_donna. The third component, ed25519-donna-tor, is the Tor-style build: ed25519.c built the way Tor builds it (src/ext/include.am): -DED25519_CUSTOMHASH, -DED25519_CUSTOMRANDOM and -DED25519_SUFFIX=_donna, so every public function is ed25519_publickey_donna, ed25519_sign_donna, ed25519_sign_open_donna, ed25519_sign_open_batch_donna and curved25519_scalarmult_basepoint_donna. Tor's digest (crypto_digest_t over libcrypto or NSS) is not a dependency a reference build can have, so the digest is the one scripts/corpus/exercisers/ed25519_donna_tor_hash.h supplies, forced in with -include: upstream's own reference SHA-512 (the code ED25519_REFHASH selects, from the unmodified ed25519-hash.h at the pinned commit, its four public names renamed donna_ref_*) wrapped in Tor's shape, a heap-allocated digest behind a one-pointer context. Upstream's own ed25519-hash-custom.h is an empty comment, so nothing in the upstream tree is changed. It stands in for Tor's digest and says nothing about what libcrypto's SHA-512 compiles to. ed25519_randombytes_unsafe_donna is the memset stub of ed25519_donna_rng.c, named through -DED25519_RNG_NAME, and must never run. Tor's own ed25519_tor.c, with its Tor-specific API (_blind_secret_key, _blind_public_key, _pubkey_from_curve25519_pubkey, ...), is the separate 2026-10-07-tor build from the Tor tree. MinGW x86 36 kept + 53 removed = 89, x64 42 + 53 = 95; Linux x86 57 + 5 = 62, x64 44 + 6 = 50 (33, 31, 36 and 30 functions of ten instructions or more). Against the same-target REFHASH build (the plain ed25519-donna component) the PicHashes at ten instructions or more are shared 29 of 33 (MinGW x86), 29 of 31 (MinGW x64), 21 of 36 (Linux x86) and 27 of 30 (Linux x64); what differs is the digest wrapper and the functions that call it (sign, hram, sign_open_batch on some targets), so a Tor-built sample matches this component on the field and group arithmetic and on the renamed public API, not on the hash.

ed25519-donna_2026-10-07-tor_gcc13_x64_e.license: BSD-3-Clause (Tor, LICENSE at the pinned commit) for ed25519_tor.c and Tor's edits; the donna code it includes is public domain (Andrew M.)
ed25519-donna_2026-10-07-tor_gcc13_x64_e.notes: Tor's own ed25519-donna glue, src/ext/ed25519/donna/ed25519_tor.c from the Tor tree at commit 8dbbbe6e86a6 (2026-10-07, configure AC_INIT 0.5.0.0-alpha-dev; the same pin serves the Tor notes of tracker issues #30 and #49), compiled with the flags of Tor's src/ext/include.am: -DED25519_CUSTOMRANDOM -DED25519_CUSTOMHASH -DED25519_SUFFIX=_donna and CFLAGS_CONSTTIME (-fwrapv), at -O2, against Tor's own copies of the donna headers in that directory (Tor's edits listed in its README.tor) and Tor's unmodified lib/ headers. This is Tor's API, not floodyberry's ed25519.c: ed25519_donna_seckey, _seckey_expand, _pubkey, _keygen, _open, _sign, _blind_secret_key, _blind_public_key, _pubkey_from_curve25519_pubkey, _scalarmult_with_group_order and _selftest, with the expanded secret key. The second component adds -DED25519_SSE2 -msse2 (what Tor's ed25519-donna-portable.h forces on 32-bit x86 whenever __SSE2__ is set). Tor's crypto entry points are supplied OUTSIDE the tree by scripts/corpus/exercisers/ed25519_tor_shim/: orconfig.h stands in for configure's output (type sizes and four feature tests), and ed25519_tor_shim.c defines crypto_digest512_new, crypto_digest_add_bytes, crypto_digest_get_digest, crypto_digest_free_, crypto_digest512 (donna's reference SHA-512 from the same tree's ed25519-hash.h, renamed corpus_sha512_*), crypto_rand_unmocked and crypto_strongest_rand (BCryptGenRandom on Windows, /dev/urandom on Linux, through corpus_os_random) and memwipe. Those shim functions, and sha512_blocks, are not Tor's code and never run. No file of the Tor tree is edited. Measured at ten instructions or more: 15 to 24 distinct PicHashes shared with the same-target ed25519-donna-tor component (floodyberry's ed25519.c with Tor's flags), 11 to 26 between the SSE2 components, and 17 to 30 per image, the shim and GCC glue left out, in none of the floodyberry components: the Tor API and the donna internals as Tor's translation unit inlines them. Counts per image are in the recipe docstring.
